board: Infineon EVAL_2.5KW_CCM_4PIN (schematic sheet name FPS27, V01, 23.07.2015)
question: Which gate network is actually populated on the EVAL_2.5KW_CCM_4PIN board, resolving the 3.3 / 20 / 10 ohm conflict?

primary_sources.identity: Infineon 2.5 kW PFC eval-board deck, 16 pp.; page 7 = Schematic sheet

driver.description: EiceDRIVER Compact 6 A isolated single-channel gate driver (coreless-transformer isolation, 1200 V, CMTI >= 100 V/ns)
driver.source_page_figure: AN_201408_PL11_027 sec.1.5 p.5; Table 2 component list p.15 (IC4 = 1EDI60N12AF '6 A isolated MOS driver'); Fig 6 schematic p.12; deck p.5 and deck p.7
driver.note: App-note body text page 5 prints the part as 'IEDI60N12AF' (typo/OCR); component list, schematic and deck all print '1EDI60N12AF'.
driver.gate_drive_bias_basis: VCC2 (output stage rail) is fed from the isolated Gate_12V / Galv_12V 12 V rail through solder jumpers J9/J10 and D6 ('short', 0 ohm) and series filter R7 (10 ohm), decoupled by C14 (1u) / C25 (100n) to SGND. VCC1 (input stage) is fed from the non-isolated 12 V rail with C32 (100n). Bias is therefore nominal 12 V, not the 10 V device-datasheet test condition.
driver.gate_drive_bias_page_figure: Fig 6 schematic p.12 (Gate_12V -> J10/J9 -> D6 -> R7 -> VCC2); deck p.7 (Galv_12V/12V -> J9/J10 -> D6 -> R7 -> VCC2); IC4 pinout Table 2 p.15
driver.output_stage_config: Out+ (pin 6) and Out- (pin 7) are tied together at the board
driver.output_stage_source: AN sec.1.5 p.5 ('In the evaluation board the two output pins are joined together'); confirmed on Fig 6 p.12 and deck p.7

turn_on_off_split.evidence_quote: In the evaluation board the two output pins are joined together. When creating a parallel design for 3 and 4pin devices two different changeable gate resistors are created. In order to keep the complexity low, the design did not take the opportunity to separate turn-on and turn-off gate resistors as this is not highly relevant for efficiency analysis.
turn_on_off_split.conflict_note: No evidence of any steering diode or of separate R_g(on)/R_g(off). A single gate-resistance element is shared by turn-on and turn-off.

gate_resistors.value_basis: full-scale rating of an adjustable trimmer (Bourns 3314G-1-200E, 20 ohm)
gate_resistors.device_configuration: 4-pin device path; paralleled by header X6 labelled 'Rg_4pin' (SPC20485)
gate_resistors.source_page_figure: Fig 6 schematic p.12; deck p.7; Table 2 component list p.15
gate_resistors.conflict_note: Schematic and component list agree on the fitted value 20 ohm. The part is a trimmer (3314G-1-200E), so 20 ohm is its maximum rating, not necessarily the operating setting. The operating setting is not stated in the schematic.

gate_resistors.value_basis: full-scale rating of an adjustable trimmer (Bourns 3314G-1-200E, 20 ohm)
gate_resistors.device_configuration: 3-pin device path; paralleled by header X7 labelled 'Rg_3pin' (SPC20485)
gate_resistors.source_page_figure: Fig 6 schematic p.12; deck p.7; Table 2 component list p.15
gate_resistors.conflict_note: Same as R9: fitted 20 ohm trimmer; operating setting not stated.

gate_resistors.value_basis: test condition annotated on the efficiency figures
gate_resistors.source_page_figure: Figure 12 and Figure 13 captions, AN p.21 ('... @ 65 kHz & 100 kHz 3.3 ohm')
gate_resistors.conflict_note: This is the only numeric gate resistance in the document tied to measured data. The captions cover both 65 kHz and 100 kHz, i.e. the same conditions as Table 3 (100 kHz, p.20). It is consistent with R9/R16 being adjustable 20 ohm trimmers set to 3.3 ohm for the measurements; it is NOT, on its own, proof of the as-shipped wiper setting, which the document does not state.

gate_source_resistor.conflict_note: No gate-source (pull-down) resistor is drawn across the DUT gate-source in Fig 6 p.12 or deck p.7. The gate elements R9/R16 connect the driver output node to the gate network, not gate to source.

parallel_series_elements.description: 2-pin header in parallel with R9; labelled 'Rg_4pin'
parallel_series_elements.source_page_figure: Fig 6 p.12; deck p.7; Table 2 p.16

parallel_series_elements.description: 2-pin header in parallel with R16; labelled 'Rg_3pin'
parallel_series_elements.source_page_figure: Fig 6 p.12; deck p.7; Table 2 p.16

parallel_series_elements.description: gate/source-sense line elements, component list says 'Placeholder for ferrite bead, 0 ohm resistor'; drawn as bead symbols between the R9/R16 network and DUT1A

excluded_designators.role: driver secondary-side VCC2 supply filter resistor, NOT a gate resistor
excluded_designators.source_page_figure: Fig 6 p.12; deck p.7; Table 2 p.15
excluded_designators.conflict_note: Net path traced: Gate_12V/Galv_12V -> J9/J10 -> D6 ('short') -> R7 (10R) -> IC4 pin 5 (VCC2), decoupled by C14 1u / C25 100n. The 10 ohm pairing with R11 in the component list is not in the gate path.

excluded_designators.role: series element in the controller VBTHL / BOFO enable divider fed from the external 12 V rail, NOT a gate resistor
excluded_designators.conflict_note: Net path traced: 12 V selected by J11 (12Vextern or Bias1 Galv_12V) -> R11 (10R) -> R18 (36k) -> BOFO/VBTHL enable tap -> R8 (10k) -> GND. Distinct sub-circuit (ICE3PCS01G bulk-voltage/enable function), not the gate drive.

unresolved.reason: No source in the bundle states the as-delivered trimmer setting; only the measurement condition 3.3 ohm is annotated.

unresolved.item: exact effective Rg if R9 and R16 are simultaneously in-circuit
unresolved.reason: The schematic connects both branches between the driver output node and the B1/B2 gate network. The app note frames them as the 3-pin and 4-pin alternatives (one per configuration), so the simultaneous-parallel value (20||20 = 10 ohm at full scale) is not asserted as populated.

verdict.confidence_reason: HIGH confidence that R9/R16 are the gate resistors, that there is no split on/off path and no steering diode, and that R7/R11 are NOT gate resistors (all directly traced on the manufacturer schematic). MEDIUM-HIGH confidence that the effective populated value under the published measured data is 3.3 ohm: the caption is the only measurement-tied numeric value, and it is consistent with 20 ohm trimmers being adjusted. The as-shipped wiper setting itself is not documented.
verdict.which_resistance_is_populated: The gate-position components are 20 ohm trimmers (R9 4-pin, R16 3-pin), and the effective gate resistance under the published efficiency/Table-3 measurements is 3.3 ohm. For a model comparison against Table 3 (100 kHz), 3.3 ohm is the populated/effective value.
verdict.model_implication: The coordinator's whole-board bound should be read at 3.3 ohm (the measurement condition), where the model's switch-only loss is a minority share of the board's measured whole-board loss. The 20 ohm figure is the trimmer's full-scale rating, not the measurement setting, so it is not evidence that the model is falsified. This is reinforced by the driver bias: the board drives ~12 V while the probe ran the model at the device's 10 V datasheet condition, which is the higher-loss direction, so the probe's 3.3 ohm share is already an upper bound.
